title: Forward Cargo Compartment Frame Feet — Detailed Inspection at Stations C24 to C31

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Detailed inspection of the frame feet at stations C24 to C31 in the forward cargo compartment, with the eddy current coverage that the repeat finding history requires and the blend history check.

sections.purpose: This task gives the detailed inspection of the frame feet at stations C24 to C31 in the forward cargo compartment, and the blend history check that establishes how much material remains at a previously reworked foot.
sections.job_setup_note: The lining and the floor panels must be removed to give access; a partial strip does not expose the inboard corner where the cracking starts. The eddy current coverage must include the radius at the inboard corner, which is the finding location, and not only the flat of the foot. A foot that has been blended before must be checked against the blend history record before any further blending is considered, because the remaining material is the limiting factor and it is not measurable in situ.
sections.procedure: 1. Remove the forward cargo compartment lining and the floor panels in zones 113 and 115. 2. Clean the frame feet and the surrounding structure and remove all protective treatment from the inspection area. WARNING: WEAR EYE AND RESPIRATORY PROTECTION DURING TREATMENT REMOVAL AND WORK WITH EXTRACTION RUNNING. 3. Do a general visual inspection of each foot at stations C24 to C31, left and right. 4. Do the eddy current inspection over the full foot area including the radius at the inboard corner. CAUTION: THE CRACKING STARTS IN THE INBOARD CORNER RADIUS AND NOT ON THE FLAT. A SCAN THAT COVERS ONLY THE FLAT WILL MISS IT. 5. Record every indication with its station, side and length. 6. For each foot with an indication, check the blend history record for previous rework at that location. 7. Where a foot has been blended twice or more, do not blend again; report it for repair assessment. 8. Where blending is permitted, blend within the limits given in the figure and re-inspect by eddy current. 9. Measure and record the blended depth. 10. Restore the protective treatment over the whole inspection area. 11. Refit the floor panels and the lining. 12. Confirm the lock actuator at the cargo door is not fouled by the refitted lining.
sections.close_out: Record every indication found, the blend depth where any blending was done, and the cumulative blend count for each foot, in the aircraft structural repair record. The cumulative count is what governs whether the next finding can be blended at all, so an unrecorded blend removes an option from the next inspection.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. On aircraft post MOD-149710 the modified stations are inspected under the general structural sampling programme instead.

safety_precautions: Wear eye and respiratory protection during treatment removal.
Work with extraction running in the cargo compartment.
Support the floor panels before the last fastener is removed.

tooling.description: Eddy current probe, 2 MHz, radius head
